hero.caption: The SR-71B Blackbird, flown by the Dryden Flight Research Center as NASA 831, slices across the snow-covered southern Sierra Nevada Mountains of California after being refueled by an Air Force tanker during a 1994 flight. SR-71B was the trainer version of the SR-71. Notice the dual cockpit to allow the instructor to fly the airplane.

images.filename: Captain Christopher Burns with the 1ST Reconnaissance Squadron is prepped for his first solo high-altitude flight by squadron aerospace physiologists before starting engines. AIRMAN - DPLA - e6db7d16a678bb68038a037ab29d58a9.jpeg
images.caption: The original finding aid described this photograph as: [Complete] Scene Caption: Captain Christopher Burns with the 1st Reconnaissance Squadron is prepped for his first solo high-altitude flight by squadron aerospace physiologists before starting engines. Airman Magazine article describes the U-2 as still being a major player in the nation's reconnaissance mission despite its 1950s' design and first flight in 1955. Capable of then flying over 70,000 feet, and now even higher thanks to a new F-118-101 engine and upgraded avionics the aircraft was awarded the Collier Trophy in 1998 by the National Aeronautic Association and named the U-2S. The U-2S now has digital capabilty and can transmit data instantaneously to analysts at Beale AFB by using a network of ground stations and satellites. (Airman Magazine/July 1999 - The Big Picture) Base: Beale Air Force Base State: California (CA) Country: United States Of America (USA) Scene Camera Operator: MSGT Dave Nolan Release Status: Released to Public

images.filename: New Child Development Center nears completion at Beale (6283634847).jpg
images.caption: Workers put the finishing touches on the roof of the new $11.2 million Child Development Center at Beale Air Force Base outside of Marysville, Calif., Oct. 25, 2011. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District is administrating construction of the 38,000 square-foot center, capable of accommodating 280 children from the ages of six weeks through five years old. Occupancy is scheduled to begin in December 2011 and a ribbon cutting ceremony is planned for the center in January 2012. (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Photo / Michael J. Nevins)
